gate_contexts.title: Rejection Improves Reliability: Training LLMs to Refuse Unknown Questions Using RL from Knowledge Feedback
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: Large Language Models (LLMs) often generate erroneous outputs, known as hallucinations, due to their limitations in discerning questions beyond their knowledge scope. While addressing hallucination has been a focal point in research, previous efforts primarily concentrate on enhancing correctness without giving due consideration to the significance of rejection mechanisms. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive examination of the role of rejection, introducing the alignment goal of model reliability along with corresponding metrics. This goal requires the model to provide accurate responses while adeptly rejecting questions exceeding its knowledge boundaries, thereby minimizing hallucinations. gate_contexts.title: Forked Diffusion for Conditional Graph Generation
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: We introduce a novel score-based diffusion framework that incorporates forking for conditional generation. In this framework, a single parent diffusion process is associated with a primary variable (e.g., structure), while multiple child diffusion processes are employed, each dedicated to a dependent variable (e.g., property). The parent process guides the co-evolution of its child processes towards segregated representation spaces. This approach allows our models to manage conditional information flow effectively, uncover intricate interactions and dependencies, and ultimately unlock new generative capabilities. Our experimental results demonstrate the significant superiority of our method over contemporary baselines in the context of conditional graph generation, highlighting the potential of forking diffusion for enhancing conditional generation tasks and inverse molecular design tas

gate_contexts.title: Knowledge Unlearning for Mitigating Privacy Risks in Language Models
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: Pretrained Language Models (LMs) memorize a vast amount of knowledge during initial pretraining, including information that may violate the privacy of personal lives and identities. Previous work addressing privacy issues for language models has mostly focused on data preprocessing and differential privacy methods, both requiring re-training the underlying LM. We propose knowledge unlearning as an alternative method to reduce privacy risks for LMs post hoc. We show that simply applying the unlikelihood training objective to target token sequences is effective at forgetting them with little to no degradation of general language modeling performances; it sometimes even substantially improves the underlying LM with just a few iterations. gate_contexts.title: ​​What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: Neural sequence models, especially transformers, exhibit a remarkable capacity for in-context learning. They can construct new predictors from sequences of labeled examples $(x, f(x))$ presented in the input without further parameter updates. We investigate the hypothesis that transformer-based in-context learners implement standard learning algorithms implicitly, by encoding context-specific parametric models in their hidden representations, and updating these implicit models as new examples appear in the context. Using linear regression as a model problem, we offer three sources of evidence for this hypothesis. First, we prove by construction that transformers can implement learning algorithms for linear models based on gradient descent and closed-form computation of regression parameters. gate_contexts.title: Unifying semi-supervised and robust learning by mixup
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: Supervised deep learning methods require cleanly labeled large-scale datasets, but collecting such data is difficult and sometimes impossible. There exist two popular frameworks to alleviate this problem: semi-supervised learning and robust learning to label noise. Although these frameworks relax the restriction of supervised learning, they are studied independently. Hence, the training scheme that is suitable when only small cleanly-labeled data are available remains unknown. In this study, we consider learning from bi-quality data as a generalization of these studies, in which a small portion of data is cleanly labeled, and the rest is corrupt. Under this framework, we compare recent algorithms for semi-supervised and robust learning. The results suggest that semi-supervised learning outperforms robust learning with noisy labels. gate_contexts.title: CausalAF: Causal Autoregressive Flow for Safety-Critical Scenes Generation
gate_contexts.abstract_excerpt: Goal-directed generation, aiming for solving downstream tasks by generating diverse data, has a potentially wide range of applications in the real world. Previous works tend to formulate goal-directed generation as a purely data-driven problem, which directly approximates the distribution of samples satisfying the goal. However, the generation ability of preexisting work is heavily restricted by inefficient sampling, especially for sparse goals that rarely show up in off-the-shelf datasets. For instance, generating safety-critical traffic scenes with the goal of increasing the risk of collision is critical to evaluate autonomous vehicles, but the rareness of such scenes is the biggest resistance. reviews.claim_boundary: The claims made in these studies primarily revolve around specific applications of new methods across defined contexts, making them less generalizable to unrelated fields or approaches. Further empirical validation is necessary to explore broader applicability.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate correctly identified the three types of preference pairs (correct/refuse/incorrect) as central to the method, producing a more precise and technically grounded artifact than baseline. It also surfaced the specific dataset scope (math questions) and GDPR-adjacent framing.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: Full_review_guided adds the preference pair detail but dilutes it with generic hedging about benchmark limitations, ending up only marginally better than baseline rather than clearly superior to the single gate.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate introduced the SDE mathematical framework detail and molecular dataset scope, both substantive additions absent from baseline. Structured feedback gate added little beyond organizational commentary.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: Single_structured_feedback largely recycled surface-level praise about writing quality without adding technical depth, making it the weakest single gate. Full_review_guided wins by combining SDE rigor with the versatility/motivation gap critique.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate uniquely surfaced the GDPR right-to-be-forgotten framing and the baseline justification gap as a concrete limitation, adding regulatory context and methodological self-awareness that neither baseline nor other gates provided.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: Single_structured_feedback and single_scientific_taste_prior both produced artifacts that are nearly identical to baseline in substance, only adding generic quality praise. Full_review_guided combines gradient ascent detail but also regresses to vague hedging, making it roughly equivalent to baseline overall.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate at least flagged the probe technique description gap as a concrete methodological weakness, adding specificity. Scientific taste and structured feedback gates produced nearly identical generic artifacts.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: None of the single gates clearly beat baseline here; all produce similarly thin artifacts. Full_review_guided wins because it combines the probe critique with the multiple-perspectives framing of the method. Single_structured_feedback is the weakest gate, adding only vague organizational praise.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate honestly reported that the improvement with noisy labels is marginal and raised the question of effectiveness, producing an artifact with better calibrated claims and more honest limitations than baseline.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: Full_review_guided adds 'modest improvements' language but also inserts vague optimism about 'significant potential for further exploration,' somewhat neutralizing the honest signal. Single_structured_feedback adds no technical depth and is the weakest condition.

per_paper.useful_gate_signal: The evaluator stress test gate introduced the causal-constraint-via-flows mechanism detail and grounded the paper in the driving scene use case, producing a more technically precise artifact with better claim calibration than baseline.
per_paper.failure_or_confound: Full_review_guided is marginally better than baseline but spends too much space on the presentation-clarity critique without adding methodological substance, making single_evaluator_stress_test the clear winner.

design_lessons: The evaluator_stress_test gate consistently provides the most actionable single-gate signal because it tends to surface concrete methodological details (e.g., specific dataset types, algorithmic pair structures, regulatory framing) rather than generic quality assessments, making it the most reliable single gate for improving artifact specificity and claim calibration.

The structured_feedback gate is the weakest single gate across papers: when isolated, it collapses to organizational commentary and surface praise, adding little technical content over baseline. It only gains value when combined with other signals in full_review_guided.

Full_review_guided wins when multiple signals are complementary (e.g., technical detail from evaluator + versatility scope from structured), but can regress toward baseline when signals conflict or dilute each other with vague hedging. The combination benefit is contingent on signal compatibility, not guaranteed by aggregation alone.

Baseline artifacts are surprisingly competitive when the abstract is already information-dense; single gates must add genuinely novel technical detail to justify their use. Generic gates that restate abstract-level information provide no measurable uplift.

Honest limitation signaling (e.g., 'marginal improvement,' 'baseline justification insufficient') from a single gate significantly improves claim_calibration and limitation_honesty scores even when novelty and experiment_quality gains are modest, suggesting that critique-oriented gate signals have disproportionate value for artifact trustworthiness.
reviews.claim_boundary: Across all six papers, the evaluator_stress_test gate is the most reliably useful single gate, producing artifacts that beat baseline in 5 of 6 cases by introducing specific technical content absent from the abstract. The structured_feedback gate fails to beat baseline when isolated, functioning only as a complement to other signals. Full_review_guided wins outright in 2 cases where multiple complementary signals exist, but the single gate wins in 3 cases where the combined signal introduces diluting hedges. These findings are limited to short mini-paper artifacts generated from title and abstract alone; results may not generalize to longer-form artifacts, other domains, or gate combinations beyond those tested. The scoring rubric used here treats technical specificity and honest limitation acknowledgment as primary value drivers, which may not reflect all downstream use cases for generated research artifacts.

interpretation: This single-gate artifact ablation generates new artifacts using only one gate-specific review signal. It therefore moves beyond post-hoc attribution. The result should be read as a small OpenReview proxy for which gates are useful in isolation and whether full review guidance still adds value over isolated gates.
claim_boundary: This is a six-paper, model-reviewed OpenReview proxy using generated mini-paper artifacts. It is closer to a causal gate ablation than post-hoc attribution, but it does not replace independent human expert ratings, real benchmark reruns, or multi-task AI Scientist-v2 matched experiments.
